reasoning: The two sets share the same skeleton: the same three stages and milestones, six pipelines, a 31-task M1 plan and near-identical file layouts. A reads as the cleaned-up, self-consistent version. B keeps stale process text in architecture.md ('adopted before M1 is built', 'a Replan of its interface task', 'five or more pipelines… All five are commands' when there are six) and a 'Replan notes' section in the plan. B has real contradictions. Its brief says agents beat the scripted player outright while EVAL-03 only requires 'not worse'. Its RunSettings says 'reinforce and ppo only with the tank' while predator-prey needs ppo. viz.Chart has no label, yet TC-70 needs one. TC-42 passes a values array of the same length as rewards, which the gae contract rejects. PL-01's FishTank omits the limited view (FISH-10). Snake/FishTank.reset_to return a bare ndarray against the team-keyed Env. with_seed is used in every entry sketch but has no contract entry. lab.main lacks --vs, --smoke and --label even though tasks verify with --smoke. B also has statistical and RL soundness problems: 'not worse' claims are corrected, which makes them easier to pass. GAE has no per-segment handling at truncation. The PPO reference uses a [-1,1] Box that SB3 clips per axis, unlike the hand-written agent. A fixes all of these explicitly: an uncorrected 'not worse' test, segmented GAE with a truncation golden case, an unbounded Box, Chart.label, with_seed, and full CLI flags. A also gives M2 and M3 checkable Exit criteria, which B lacks. A's task packets are more complete. Its M1-T06 packet includes Transition, StepResult, TeamSpec, SOLO, create_run, GameRecording and OpponentPool; B's omits them all. B's M1-T02 packet omits with_seed even though its acceptance tests it. A's sizes are also more realistic: DQN spine M, Snake S, CNN S, versus all XS in B. A's main weaknesses are a heavy M1 interface that stubs M2/M3 symbols, and very large shared PL-01 tables.

strengths: Statistically sound claim handling: 'not worse' tested uncorrected, with TC-23(c) proving a larger family never helps it pass
GAE contract and TC-42(b) handle truncation segments correctly; the PPO reference action Box is unbounded so it matches the hand-written agent
Roadmap gives M2 and M3 checkable Exit criteria
Spine packets carry every type they need (e.g. M1-T06 has Transition, StepResult, create_run, OpponentPool)
Realistic task sizes (DQN spine M, Snake S, CNN S), and the T26→T27 file conflict is serialized and explained
No stale process narration; brief open question resolved
weaknesses: Brief softens the user's 'beats scripted' bar to 'matches or beats' (consistent with the spec, but a deliberate dilution)
M1 interface freezes and stubs many M2/M3 symbols (FishTank, PPOAgent, PredatorPrey) that no M1 task uses
PL-01's step table mixes all three stages' steps, so M1 builders read lots of irrelevant rows
Tank/predator TCs still say 'one correction over all the report's claims', a small wording mismatch with the greater-only rule
